submission.natural_language_explanation: The pole fires when text attributes a restricted or alternative identity to something: minimizers before a predicate noun ('just/simply/merely/only a X', 'a mere X', 'nothing/little/no more than a X', 'essentially/basically a X'), limiting adverbs of proportion ('primarily/mainly/mostly/partly of'), contrastive-alternative pivots ('not X but Y', 'X rather than Y', 'instead of', 'as opposed to', 'versus', 'prefer X to Y'), and more weakly source/composition/scope predications ('originated from', 'composed of', 'based on', 'confined to'). The peak sits on the pivot token itself -- the 'than', 'but' or 'versus', the 'of'/'to' of the substitute phrase, or the determiner opening the downgraded noun phrase -- and the pole stays near zero when the same words lack that function: temporal 'just now', quantifier 'only a few', additive 'simply put', plain contrast 'small but clean', numeric 'more than fifty', plain copula 'is a X', or set exclusion 'except/apart from'.

adversarial_test_results.detail: Set exclusion 'apart from' is explicitly predicted inactive even though it names an alternative member of a set.

Today the festival attracts visitors from neighbouring towns, yet the organisers insist that the core of the evening has not changed: a shared meal, a short walk, and the same request for rain.
